question: If random variable X follows binomial distribution with parameter n and p with mean 15 and variance 10, then the value of mode is
solution:
The correct answer is **46/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The mode of a **binomial distribution** is the value of x that has the highest probability of occurrence.
 
• In a binomial distribution with parameters n and p, the mode can be found using the formula: mode = floor(n * p), where "floor" represents the greatest integer less than or equal to the argument.
 
• The **mean and variance** of a binomial distribution can be used to find the values of n and p, and subsequently the mode.
 
• The mode, mean and variance are important characteristics of a distribution that describe the shape, central tendency and spread of the data.
 
• Understanding the properties of binomial distribution and how to find the mode, mean and variance is important in many areas of statistics and data analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **mode of a binomial distribution** is the value of x that has the highest probability of occurrence.
 
• In a binomial distribution with parameters n and p, the mode can be found using the formula:
 
• **mode = floor(n * p)**
 
• Where "floor" represents the greatest integer less than or equal to the argument.
 
• Given that the mean of the distribution is 15 and the variance is 10, we can find n and p by solving two equations.
 
• The mean of a binomial distribution is equal to n * p, and the variance is equal to n * p * (1 - p).
 
• Solving for n and p and substituting into the formula for the mode, we get 46/3 as the answer.
